skills.trigger: When evaluating chest X-rays (especially lateral views) for causes of heart failure, pericardial disease, or unexplained calcifications near the cardiac silhouette.
steps: Inspect the lateral chest X-ray specifically for a distinct, curvilinear calcification that outlines the anterior and inferior borders of the heart.

Distinguish constrictive calcified pericarditis from other calcifications by confirming the linear shape follows the pericardial contour rather than appearing as a focal mass (aneurysm), ring-like structure at the AV groove (mitral annulus), or diffuse parenchymal opacity.

skills.trigger: When identifying pacemaker lead placement on frontal and lateral chest radiographs to confirm device integrity and positioning.
steps: Trace the pacemaker lead from the generator pocket through the superior vena cava into the right atrium and across the tricuspid valve.

Confirm right ventricular placement by verifying the lead tip projects over the cardiac apex on the frontal view and lies anteriorly against the lower sternum on the lateral view; distinguish from left ventricular placement which would typically course posteriorly via the coronary sinus or appear malpositioned.
